summary: [¶] (o) On 03.01.2022 and 04.01.2022, CTUIL raised Bill-1 and Bilateral Bill for January 2022. On 07.01.2022, SEIL wrote an e-mail to CTUIL _inter alia_ stating that SEIL was in receipt of a credit amount of Rs. 19.40 crore towards Project P1 Transmission Charges (Bill-2) for the period from April 2021 to June 2021. On 06.12.2021, SEIL had written to CTUIL requesting that the credit amount be remitted directly to SEIL’s account instead of being adjusted in monthly bills. On 03.01.2022, SEIL received Bill-1 for the untied quantum from SEIL’s Project P1 and Project P2 and tied-up quantum for Project P2, amounting to Rs. 15.90 crore. As there has been a delay in crediting the amount to SEIL, SEIL proposed to adjust the transmission charges payable by SEIL for the billing month of January 2022. Accordingly, SEIL sought CTUIL’s confirmation regarding whether Transmission Charges payable for SEIL’s Project P2 for January 2022 can be adjusted against the receivable amount qua SEIL Project P1, and whether SEIL is eligible for availing TDS and rebate on the payable amount while adjusting the amounts (which is Rs. 15.35 crore). After adjustment of transmission charges for January 2022, the balance amount payable by CTUIL is Rs. 4.05. crore. [¶] vi. Accordingly, SEIL issued a debit note towards interest/Late Payment Surcharge amounting to Rs. 2,26,33,048/- for the delayed period computed on the basis of LPS payment methodology mentioned in the Sharing Regulations 2020. [¶] (t) On 04.04.2022, SEIL wrote to CTUIL and stated that to date, the interest amount had not been remitted by CTUIL to SEIL. Accordingly, CTUIL was requested to pay the interest amount of Rs. 2,26,33,048/- within 15 days. In the event of CTUIL’s failure to release the aforesaid amount, SEIL would be constrained to initiate appropriate legal action, and such failure would be construed as noncompliance with the relevant Regulations and other applicable laws. [¶] (v) SEIL ought to be compensated and restituted for the delay in reimbursement/refund/adjustment of excess transmission charges paid to CTUIL. The Hon`ble Supreme Court in _**State of Rajasthan vs. J.K Synthetics Ltd. [reported as (2011) 12 SCC 518]**_ categorically held that even if there is no provision, the court can direct payment of interest by way of restitution. This principle was also upheld by the Hon`ble Madras High Court in _**S. Parameswaran vs. Union of India and Another [reported as 2006 SCC On Line Mad 455]**_ wherein the Hon`ble Madras High Court reiterated the decision of the Hon`ble Supreme Court in _**Sandvik Asia Ltd. vs. Commissioner of Income Tax I, Pune & Ors. Reported as [(2006) 2 SCC 508].**_ [¶] b) Even otherwise, the CTUIL is also not levying interest in case after the revised RTA, there has been any under-recovery of transmission charges due to the absence of a specific regulatory provision. If the present Petition is allowed, interest would be recoverable from other DICs. [¶] tranches, with the last tranche on 8.2.2022. Thus, there has been a delay of 252 days in the adjustment of the revised transmission charges from 01.06.2021 to 08.02.2022 for which the Petitioner needs to be compensated. The Petitioner has submitted that on 11.2.2022, it issued a debit note for interest/Late Payment Surcharge amounting to Rs. 2,26,33,048/- for the delayed period, computed on the basis of the LPS payment methodology mentioned in the Sharing Regulations 2020, to CTUIL.
